userStories.title: Gated project thread create, cap update and archive, and the archive cancel after commit
userStories.description:
**Goal** — Gate the three project thread writes and make archive cancellation safe after deferred execution commits.

**Motivation** — 5a to 5d-1 gated 97 routes. The thread writes still bypass the engine on REST: a policy `thread.message.send → agent` makes nothing wait, because no thread route asks the gate.

**Approach** — The following design instructions apply verbatim:
- **Request checks the handler makes today stay before the gate**, so they answer as today and open no request. The thread handlers make none today except `canOperate` (below); every check runs in the service, so it runs inside the command, at once or after approval, and a failing check settles the request `failed`. This is 5a's rule.
- **`canOperate` is the requester's at execution.** The project handlers compute `canOperate` today with a private helper (`permissions.can(principal, <key>, { projectId })`). Each command computes it again when it runs, as 5d-1's schedule commands compute `canAdminister`. The helper and the controller's `PermissionService` leave `ThreadsController`, which gains `ApprovalRouteGate`. (Their final removal belongs to US-005; retain them for remaining ungated handlers now.)
- **The archive answers the archived thread from the command.** The project and workspace archive handlers answer `threads.get(…)` after the archive today. The archive commands run the archive and then the read, and answer the read, so a deferred archive stores the thread detail as its result.
- **The archive cancel is deferred.** `ThreadsService.archive` and `WorkspaceThreadsService.archive` hand their `fleetJobs.cancel(…)` (with its `ConflictAppException` catch) to `AfterCommitService.defer(task)`, and run it at once when `defer` answers false. Both services gain `AfterCommitService` (last constructor parameter) and a `private readonly logger = new Logger(<the class>.name)` field. `AfterCommitService` is global (`PermissionsModule`). `AfterCommitService.scope` runs its tasks with no catch, and a throw there escapes the execution's commit, so the deferred task catches and logs every failure (Design snippet); the immediate path keeps today's behaviour (a non-conflict failure propagates). The commands do not use `routeCommand`'s `afterCommit` hook, because the cancel belongs to the service and must also run on the immediate path. (Implement the project service in this story; workspace follows in US-006.)
- **A deferred create that loses the unique feature race fails the request.** `ThreadsService.create` catches the `repo_feature` unique violation and throws 409 `threads.featureTaken`. Inside the execution transaction the violation aborts the transaction, and the request settles `failed`. 5d-1's deferred dispatch behaves the same way.
- **The frozen input is ids, slugs and the validated body.** Project inputs carry `slug`, so the execution locks the slug to the request's project (`lockProjectSlug`). Workspace inputs carry the thread id, and the body where there is one.
- **Each gating story removes its own `PENDING_GATE_ROUTES` rows.** US-001 relaxes the exact gated-route count to a lower bound (at least 97), and the allowlist count case to the `gate-secret` count. US-009 restores both exactly and removes the `gate-fleet` label.
- **Only the HTTP handlers change.** Gated handlers keep their parameters, in order. This limits the gated entry points, not the supporting service and commands changes explicitly assigned here; assistant/MCP primary commands and SSE routes remain unchanged.

**Interface** — Create `ThreadRouteCommands`, `THREAD_ROUTE_VARIANTS` in `fleet/threads/thread-route.commands.ts`. Each row is one `routeCommand`; principal is rebuilt by ActorPrincipalLoader.
| Route | Key | Scope | Variant | Input | Run |
| POST /projects/:slug/threads | thread.create | project | rest:threads.create | { slug, projectId, thread: parseBody(CreateThreadDto, …) } | threads.create(projectId, principal.id, thread) |
| PATCH /projects/:slug/threads/:id | thread.cap.update | project | rest:threads.update | { slug, projectId, id, patch: parseBody(UpdateThreadDto, …) } | threads.updateCap(projectId, id, principal.id, patch.maxCostUsd, <canOperate>) |
| POST /projects/:slug/threads/:id/archive | thread.archive | project | rest:threads.archive | { slug, projectId, id } | threads.archive(projectId, id, principal.id, <canOperate>), then threads.get(projectId, id) |
`<canOperate>` = `(await permissions.can(principal, <the row's key>, { projectId })).allowed` at execution. Every body-returning command declares `toResult: (result) => result` unless the row says otherwise; a command whose route answers `{}` runs the service, answers `{}` and declares `toResult: (result) => result`. On `executed` the handler answers `JsonResponse.Ok(outcome.result)`. Id and string members are read with `parseRouteInput`; a body member with `parseBody` of the route's DTO (a missing body member is parsed as `{}`).

```ts
const outcome = await this.routeGate.run<ChatThreadRecord>({ key: 'thread.cap.update', variant: THREAD_ROUTE_VARIANTS.update, projectId: ctx.project.id, input: { slug: ctx.project.slug, projectId: ctx.project.id, id, patch: dto } });
if (outcome.status === 'pending') throw new ApprovalPending(outcome.request);
return JsonResponse.Ok(outcome.result);
```
The deferred archive cancel:
```ts
const cancel = async () => {
  try { await this.fleetJobs.cancel(userId, projectId, jobId, true); }
  catch (error) { if (!(error instanceof ConflictAppException)) throw error; }
};
// After commit the archive is done: a failed cancel is logged, never thrown out of the commit.
const deferred = () => cancel().catch((error: unknown) => this.logger.warn(`archive cancel of job ${jobId} failed: ${String(error)}`));
if (!this.afterCommit.defer(deferred)) await cancel();
```
A create body is `{ kind: 'REPO', repoId: world.repoId, feature: <unique>, title: <unique>, backend: { kind: 'native', model: 'm1' } }`. ThreadsModule imports ApprovalEngineModule and AuthRepositoryModule and provides ThreadRouteCommands; commands constructor takes ApprovalCommandRegistry, ThreadsService, PermissionService and ActorPrincipalLoader as ScheduleRouteCommands does. ThreadsController gains ApprovalRouteGate last, becoming (threads, permissions, routeGate). Each gated handler gains @ApprovalGated() and keeps @Requires, @HttpCode and @ApiResponses. ThreadsService gains AfterCommitService last; update every direct service construction with new AfterCommitService() as seventh argument. Extend the DB-free module spec to resolve ThreadRouteCommands, update constructor metadata and controller gate mapping cases, and move service invocation assertions into the commands spec. Temporarily assert only the 11 gate-secret rows, remove the old project-create gate-fleet assertion, and use at least 97 gated routes.

**Scope** — In: the three routes, project archive deferral, commands/DI/controller/service tests and their three allowlist removals. Out: remaining project routes (US-002–US-005), workspace archive deferral (US-006), and final 115/OpenAPI closure (US-009).
- Retrying an archive cancel that failed after commit; the deferred task logs it (Design).
- Running a service's domain checks before a request opens, beyond the workspace pre-read in Design.
- Changing any catalog default: these keys stay `none`.

AC-11 [unit] When ThreadsService.archive('p1', 't1', 'u1', true) receives job j1 from the repository, then inside AfterCommitService.scope it calls fleetJobs.cancel('u1', 'p1', 'j1', true) only after the scope callback returns, while outside any scope it calls cancel before archive answers.

AC-14 [unit] When fleetJobs.cancel rejects a non-conflict error during ThreadsService.archive('p1', 't1', 'u1', true), then inside AfterCommitService.scope archive resolves without throwing and logger.warn is called once, while outside any scope the same rejection propagates.

userStories.description:

**Only the HTTP handlers change.** Gated handlers keep their parameters, in order. This limits the gated entry points; the route-command registration and tests assigned here are also in scope, while non-HTTP primary commands and SSE routes are unchanged.
Binding ruling: `POST /projects/:slug/threads/:id/plan` and `/run` gate under `thread.plan` and `thread.run` only. Both routes also require `fleet.job.dispatch`, but a policy naming `fleet.job.dispatch` does not make them wait (Out of Scope), as 5c-1's edge keys.
Binding ruling: a deferred send, plan, run or discard places its job inside the execution transaction, as 5d-1's deferred dispatch does.

**Interface** — Extend existing ThreadRouteCommands and THREAD_ROUTE_VARIANTS with plan/run, and extend its existing commands spec.
| Route | Key | Scope | Variant | Input | Run |
| POST /projects/:slug/threads/:id/plan | thread.plan | project | rest:threads.plan | { slug, projectId, id, plan: parseBody(PlanThreadDto, …) } | threads.plan(projectId, id, principal.id, plan, <canOperate>) |
| POST /projects/:slug/threads/:id/run | thread.run | project | rest:threads.run | { slug, projectId, id, run: parseBody(RunThreadDto, …) } | threads.run(projectId, id, principal.id, run, <canOperate>) |
`<canOperate>` = `(await permissions.can(principal, <the row's key>, { projectId })).allowed` at execution; principal is the rebuilt UserPrincipal | AgentPrincipal. Every body-returning command declares `toResult: (result) => result` unless the row says otherwise; a command whose route answers `{}` runs the service, answers `{}` and declares `toResult: (result) => result`. On `executed` the handler answers `JsonResponse.Ok(outcome.result)`. Id and string members are read with `parseRouteInput`; a body member with `parseBody` of the route's DTO (a missing body member is parsed as `{}`). Each gated handler gains @ApprovalGated(), keeps @Requires (including fleet.job.dispatch), @HttpCode and @ApiResponses, throws new ApprovalPending(outcome.request) on pending, and forwards executed results. Domain checks stay inside the service so stale specPublished fails execution with 409 threads.notPublished. Remove only plan/run from PENDING_GATE_ROUTES. A plannable thread is a thread of the agent with specPublished true and runnerId an online runner. A completed plan is a FleetJob with command PLAN, the thread's threadId, repoId and feature, planFrom the thread's specPath and state COMPLETED, following permissions-project-threads.integration.spec.ts.

**Scope** — In: plan/run gate commands, handlers, registration/run cases and isolated HTTP integration tests. Out: session operations (US-003), publish/discard (US-004), message preparation (US-005), and final contracts (US-009).
- A policy naming `fleet.job.dispatch` on `POST /projects/:slug/threads/:id/plan` and `/run`: they gate under `thread.plan` and `thread.run` only (ruling 2026-10-29).
- A transaction timeout other than Prisma's default for the execution transaction: a deferred send, plan, run, publish or discard places its job inside it (ruling 2026-10-29; publish places on its new-job branch as discard does).
acceptanceCriteria: AC-1 [integration] Given an agent holding project.read, thread.plan, thread.run and fleet.job.dispatch in P and its plannable thread with specPublished true and an online runner, when it posts {} to /api/projects/web/threads/:id/plan under a thread.plan wait policy, then it answers 202 with data matching { permissionKey: 'thread.plan', projectId: <P's id> } and no PLAN FleetJob exists for the thread.

AC-2 [integration] When root approves a newly opened equivalent of AC-1's request, then exactly one PLAN FleetJob exists for the thread with requestedById equal to the agent's id and request.result.job.id equal to its id.
AC-3 [integration] When root approves the agent's pending plan after specPublished was set false while it waited, then the request settles failed and no PLAN job exists for the thread.

AC-4 [integration] Given a plannable thread whose latest PLAN job is COMPLETED, when the agent posts {} to /api/projects/web/threads/:id/run under a thread.run wait policy, then it answers 202 with data.permissionKey thread.run.
AC-5 [integration] When root approves a newly opened equivalent of AC-4's request, then one RUN FleetJob exists for the thread.
AC-6 [integration] When the agent posts plan on a plannable thread with a wait policy for fleet.job.dispatch only, then it answers 201 and writes no ApprovalRequest row.
AC-7 [unit] When ThreadRouteCommands.onModuleInit runs, then the registry answers thread.plan for rest:threads.plan and thread.run for rest:threads.run.

AC-8 [unit] When rest:threads.run runs as principal a1 whose can('thread.run') is allowed with input { slug: 'web', projectId: 'p1', id: 't1', run: { maxCostUsd: 3 } }, then it calls threads.run('p1', 't1', 'a1', { maxCostUsd: 3 }, true).
